tagline: Global leader in semiconductors delivering data solutions for memory and storage, powering AI and cloud infrastructure.
hero_kpi_rationale: Revenue from the CMBU segment, focused on HBM memory for data centers and AI, has become the primary driver of growth and profitability, increasing 257% in 2025, fueled by exponentially rising AI demand.

kpis.name: AI and Cloud Segment Revenue (CMBU)
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the Compute and Networking Business Unit providing high-performance memory for AI servers and data centers.
kpis.description: The Compute and Networking Business Unit (CMBU) saw revenue increase from $3.8B in 2024 to $13.5B in 2025, driven by demand for HBM, high-capacity DIMMs, and low-power DRAM for cloud servers.
kpis.signal: Explosive CMBU revenue growth driven by HBM demand for AI.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue remaining after deducting cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved from 22% in 2024 to 40% in 2025, driven by higher selling prices, a shift toward premium products such as HBM, and cost reductions.
kpis.signal: Dramatic rebound in gross margin due to pricing power and product mix.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin increased from 5% in 2024 to 26% in 2025, reflecting improved pricing, favorable product mix, and cost discipline.
kpis.signal: Return to strong operating profitability following the 2023 downturn.

kpis.name: R&D Investment (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Amount invested in research and development relative to revenue.
kpis.description: R&D expenses increased in absolute terms ($3.8B in 2025 vs $3.4B in 2024), but their share of revenue declined due to strong revenue growth.
kpis.signal: Decline in R&D-to-revenue ratio despite higher absolute spending.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total sales generated by the company.
kpis.description: Total revenue surged 49% in 2025, rising from $25.1B to $37.4B, driven by higher DRAM and NAND prices and volumes.
kpis.signal: Massive growth driven by AI-related memory demand.

kpis.name: Total Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Total headcount was 54,000 employees in 2025, stable compared to 2024, suggesting improved productivity.
kpis.signal: Stable headcount despite growth, indicating productivity gains.

kpis.name: CMBU Revenue (AI and Cloud Memory)
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by the Cloud and HPC segment dedicated to AI and cloud data center servers.
kpis.description: The CMBU, which supplies HBM and high-capacity memory for AI servers, generated $13.5B in revenue in 2025 (36% of total), up from $3.8B in 2024 (15% of total).
kpis.signal: CMBU is the primary AI growth engine, contributing 36% of total revenue.

kpis.name: Total Revenue and Demand
kpis.explanation: Total revenue reflecting strong demand for memory products, particularly those related to AI and data centers.
kpis.description: Total revenue reflects sustained strong demand, with 49% growth in 2025, primarily driven by AI and data center demand.
kpis.signal: Revenue growth aligned with exceptional demand for AI memory.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury).
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + share buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net Income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net Income of $8.539 Bn in the last fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.description: Operating Income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Operating Income of $9.77 Bn in the last fiscal year (FY2025).

risks.title: Foreign Exchange Rate Fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to foreign exchange rate fluctuations on significant operations. The report quantifies exposure at $572 million in the event of a 10% depreciation of foreign currencies.

risks.title: Technology Dependence
risks.score_rationale: The company is highly dependent on rapid technological evolution to maintain competitiveness in semiconductor memory.

risks.title: Increased Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a highly competitive market with other memory manufacturers, which could lead to pricing pressure and margin compression.

risks.title: Supply Chain Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to risks related to semiconductor manufacturing and the global supply chain.

risks.title: Geopolitical Regulatory Risks
risks.score_rationale: The report cites the significant impact of the 2023 decision by China's Cyberspace Administration (CAC) restricting sales of Micron products in China. This continues to affect domestic Chinese data center markets.

risks.title: Cybersecurity Risks
risks.score_rationale: Cybersecurity is explicitly mentioned in the 10-K regarding sales restrictions in China and general data security risks.

ai_positioning.summary: Micron explicitly positions AI as a primary growth driver. The 2025 10-K mentions AI-driven demand approximately 10 times in the MD&A. The company has redirected its DRAM supply toward data center and hyperscale markets powered by AI, particularly for HBM products. The CMBU (Compute and Networking Business Unit), specialized in high-performance AI memory, surged to $13.5B (+257% YoY), representing 36% of total revenue in 2025 versus 15% in 2024.
evidence: MD&A: 'AI-driven demand is accelerating and is outpacing industry supply'
MD&A: 'we shifted a portion of our DRAM supply to the data center and hyperscale cloud markets to meet the strong demand fueled by AI, with emphasis on HBM products'
MD&A: 'Sales of DRAM products increased 62% primarily due to a low-40% range increase in average selling prices and a mid-teen percentage increase in bit shipments' (driven by AI demand)
CMBU revenue increased 257% 'driven by accelerating AI demand in cloud server markets for HBM, high-capacity dual in-line memory modules (DIMMs), and low-power server DRAM'

MD&A: 'The pivot to higher-growth segments, together with our strong execution, robust overall industry DRAM demand, and constrained supply, has led to improved profitability across our DRAM portfolio'
